3.modern-en: Quarrels with Titania over a changeling boy she refuses to give up. Overhears Helena being rejected by Demetrius and orders Puck to use a magic flower on Demetrius's eyes so he will love Helena.

4.modern-en: Squeezes the love juice on Titania's eyes while she sleeps, hoping she will fall in love with the first creature she sees upon waking.

6.modern-en: Discovers Puck anointed the wrong Athenian's eyes. Applies the love juice to Demetrius while he sleeps to fix the mistake. When all four lovers are in chaos, orders Puck to create a fog and sort everything out.

7.modern-en: Having obtained the changeling boy from the enchanted Titania, releases her from the spell. They reconcile and dance together. Blesses the sleeping lovers.

9.modern-en: Arrives at Theseus's palace with Titania to bless the marriages. Leads the fairies in a song of blessing over the house.

3.modern-en: Refuses to give Oberon the changeling boy, explaining she keeps him in honor of his dead mother who was her devoted follower. Their quarrel has disrupted the natural seasons.

4.modern-en: Falls asleep in her bower, unaware that Oberon applies the love flower to her eyes.

5.modern-en: Wakes to the sound of Bottom singing and, under the spell, falls deeply in love with him despite his donkey head. Orders her fairies to attend to his every wish.

7.modern-en: Wakes from the enchantment, horrified to find herself cradling a donkey-headed man. Reconciles with Oberon and they dance.

9.modern-en: Joins Oberon at the palace to bless the newlyweds' house.

3.modern-en: Meets a fairy and boasts of his tricks. Is sent by Oberon to fetch the magic love flower and to anoint the Athenian youth's eyes.

4.modern-en: Applies the love juice to Lysander's eyes by mistake, thinking he is the Athenian Oberon described.

5.modern-en: Transforms Bottom's head into a donkey's head, scattering the other craftsmen in terror. Leads Bottom to Titania's bower.

6.modern-en: Reports to Oberon that Titania is in love with a monster. Corrects the mistake by anointing Demetrius's eyes. When the four lovers descend into chaos, creates a fog and leads them astray until they fall asleep, then applies the antidote to Lysander.

7.modern-en: Removes the donkey head from Bottom at Oberon's command.

9.modern-en: Delivers the epilogue directly to the audience, asking for applause and forgiveness if the play has offended.

2.modern-en: Dominates the casting meeting, wanting to play every part. Assigned the role of Pyramus in the play for the Duke's wedding.

5.modern-en: His head is transformed into a donkey's head by Puck. When Titania wakes and falls in love with him, he accepts her devotion with comic self-assurance, attended by fairy servants.

7.modern-en: Wakes after the spell is broken, thinking it was all a wonderful dream. Tries to describe 'Bottom's Dream' but finds it beyond words.

8.modern-en: Returns to his fellow actors just in time, having been missing and feared dead. They joyfully prepare for the performance.

9.modern-en: Performs the role of Pyramus in the hilariously bad play before the Duke's court, dying dramatically on stage.

epithet.en: Daughter of Egeus, in love with Lysander

1.modern-en: Defies her father Egeus and Duke Theseus by refusing to marry Demetrius. Faces death or a convent as punishment. Plans to elope with Lysander through the forest.

4.modern-en: Falls asleep in the forest beside Lysander. Wakes alone to find him gone and searches for him in terror.

6.modern-en: Finds Lysander now declaring love for Helena due to the enchantment. Believes Helena has stolen him and becomes furious, nearly coming to blows with her former friend.

7.modern-en: Wakes beside Lysander, whose love for her has been restored by Puck's antidote. Found by Theseus and granted permission to marry Lysander.

9.modern-en: Watches the craftsmen's play alongside the other newlyweds at Theseus's palace.

epithet.en: A young Athenian in love with Hermia

1.modern-en: Argues before Theseus that he is as worthy as Demetrius. Plans to elope with Hermia to his aunt's house beyond Athenian law. Tells Helena the plan.

4.modern-en: Falls asleep beside Hermia in the forest. Puck mistakenly anoints his eyes, causing him to fall madly in love with Helena when she wakes him.

6.modern-en: Under the spell, pursues Helena and rejects Hermia. Nearly fights Demetrius over Helena. Led astray by Puck's fog until he collapses in exhaustion.

7.modern-en: Wakes with his love for Hermia restored. Found by Theseus and given permission to marry her.

9.modern-en: Married to Hermia, watches the performance of Pyramus and Thisbe at the palace.

epithet.en: A young Athenian in love with Demetrius

1.modern-en: Learns of Hermia and Lysander's elopement plan. Decides to tell Demetrius, hoping to win his gratitude by leading him to Hermia in the forest.

3.modern-en: Follows Demetrius into the forest despite his harsh rejection. He tells her he does not love her, but she persists.

4.modern-en: Stumbles upon the sleeping Lysander and wakes him. Is bewildered when he suddenly declares passionate love for her, believing he is mocking her.

6.modern-en: Now pursued by both Lysander and the enchanted Demetrius, she believes they are conspiring with Hermia to humiliate her.

7.modern-en: Wakes beside Demetrius, whose love for her is now permanent. Found by Theseus and accepted as Demetrius's bride.

9.modern-en: Married to Demetrius, enjoys the entertainment at the Duke's palace.

epithet.en: A young Athenian, favored by Egeus

1.modern-en: Backed by Egeus as the suitor for Hermia. Urges Lysander to give up his claim.

3.modern-en: Enters the forest pursuing Hermia. Cruelly rejects Helena, who follows him despite his insults.

4.modern-en: Continues searching the forest for Hermia. Falls asleep exhausted.

6.modern-en: Wakes with the love juice on his eyes and falls in love with Helena. Competes with Lysander for Helena's affection, nearly fighting him.

7.modern-en: Wakes still in love with Helena (the enchantment is permanent for him). Tells Theseus his love for Hermia has melted away.

9.modern-en: Married to Helena, comments on the craftsmen's performance.

1.modern-en: Prepares for his wedding to Hippolyta. Hears Egeus's complaint and tells Hermia she must obey her father's choice, face death, or become a nun.

7.modern-en: Discovers the four sleeping lovers in the forest during a hunt. Overrules Egeus and allows the lovers to marry as they choose.

9.modern-en: Chooses the craftsmen's play as wedding entertainment despite Philostrate's warnings. Watches with generous good humor, commenting on the power of imagination.

epithet.en: Queen of the Amazons, betrothed to Theseus

1.modern-en: Anticipates her wedding to Theseus, noting how quickly the days will pass.

7.modern-en: Present when the lovers are discovered in the forest. Marvels at their strange account.

9.modern-en: Watches the craftsmen's play. Expresses more sympathy for the amateur performers than her husband does.

1.modern-en: Brings his daughter before Theseus, demanding she marry Demetrius or face the ancient Athenian penalty of death. Accuses Lysander of bewitching her.

7.modern-en: Present when the lovers are found, but Theseus overrules his objections and allows Hermia to marry Lysander.

epithet.en: A carpenter, director of the craftsmen's play

2.modern-en: Organizes the casting meeting for the play of Pyramus and Thisbe. Assigns roles to the craftsmen despite Bottom's attempts to play every part.

5.modern-en: Tries to rehearse the play in the forest but is scattered when Puck transforms Bottom's head.

8.modern-en: Despairs that the play cannot go on without Bottom, then rejoices at his return.

9.modern-en: Performs the prologue before the Duke's court, mangling the punctuation and accidentally insulting the audience.

2.modern-en: Cast as the Lion. Worries he is slow to learn his lines but is reassured he only needs to roar.

9.modern-en: Performs the Lion at the Duke's court, carefully explaining he is only Snug the joiner so the ladies won't be frightened.

2.modern-en: Reluctantly cast as Thisbe, protesting that he has a growing beard and shouldn't play a woman.

5.modern-en: Present at the forest rehearsal. Performs Thisbe's lines during the practice.

8.modern-en: Present when Bottom returns and the play can proceed.

9.modern-en: Performs Thisbe in the play before the court, delivering a comically overwrought death scene.

2.modern-en: Cast as Pyramus's father, later reassigned to play the Wall.

5.modern-en: Present at the forest rehearsal. Raises concerns about bringing a wall on stage.

9.modern-en: Performs the Wall in the play, holding up his fingers to represent the chink through which the lovers whisper.

2.modern-en: Cast as Thisbe's mother, later reassigned to play Moonshine.

9.modern-en: Performs Moonshine in the play, carrying a lantern and a dog. Struggles against the audience's heckling.
